transcript:
[00:00] Samira (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Samira from Redwood, Diego our solutions engineer, Priya from CS, Ben from security. And from NovusHealth?
[00:08] Marta (Novus): Marta here, Jamal, Rina, Tom and Lina are on. We got the calendar, thanks.
[00:13] Samira: Awesome. Goal today: walk through data handling, prompt retention, KMS integration, and confirm the \"no training on customer data\" commitment and how it maps to your compliance needs. We'll also go over RBAC/SSO and logs. We'll be somewhat technical.
[00:25] Diego (SE): Hi all. I'll jump into the runtime and how inference flows for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Quick note: words in this transcript may be a bit off — apologies ahead.
[00:33] Jamal (Novus): That's fine. We're primarily focused on Dedicated or Private. We can't have PHI leaving our cloud.
[00:39] Ben (Redwood): Understood — we'll be explicit about data egress, logs, and key management.
[00:44] Samira: First question from us: do you have a compliance baseline you're aligning to? SOC 2? ISO? Any specific retention policy?
[00:50] Marta: SOC 2 Type II plus ISO 27001 in progress. We also have a 7-year medical record retention rule but for ML logs we want shorter.
[00:58] Samira: Got it. From Redwood's side, for Dedicated we can maintain zero egress — compute stays in your VPC or our dedicated pool under contract. For Private, the control plane can be customer-hosted.
[01:08] Rina: Can you explain how prompts are stored? We want to ensure prompts containing PHI are not used to train any future models and are either ephemeral or pseudonymized.
[01:16] Diego: Absolutely. Short version — by default Hosted API keeps request logs for X days for debugging and billing. We offer an opt-in to \"no-retain/no-train\" mode where request bodies are not persisted beyond ephemeral cache and are excluded from any training pipelines. For Dedicated, you can configure log sink to your S3/GCS and set lifecycle rules; for Private, logs are fully under customer control.
[01:35] Jamal: When you say ephemeral cache — is that the KV cache you mentioned? Is any content kept in RAM only?
[01:41] Diego: The KV cache (we sometimes call it prefix or context cache) is in memory for active sessions to speed up generation; by default it's not written to disk unless configured. However for safety and audit we do keep audit logs of request metadata (time, model, token counts, request id) — but we can redact or pseudonymize the text content in those logs per contract.
[02:00] Tom (Legal): We need explicit language: no-derivative-training and no-human-review without customer consent. Is that feasible?
[02:07] Samira: Yes. Our standard DPA has a clause that customer content is not used to improve models. We can provide contract language and a one-way attestation. We'll circulate the DPA and SOC 2 artifacts.
[02:15] Marta: What about accidental human review via quality teams?
[02:18] Ben: We have limited escalation where content might surface for debugging. That's controlled by RBAC and audit trails; only named roles with JIT approval can see redacted content. For Novus, we can lock that down to zero.
[02:29] Rina: I want to dive into encryption and KMS. How do we rotate keys; are keys in our KMS?
[02:34] Diego: For Dedicated you can bring your own KMS (BYOK) — we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault. You store the master key; Redwood uses envelope encryption for artifacts and stores only encrypted blobs in object storage. We support key rotation without re-encrypting historical blobs by using an encrypted key-encryption-key approach.
[02:52] Jamal: Are model weights ever encrypted at rest differently?
[02:56] Ben: Model weights shipped to Dedicated nodes are encrypted in transit, and at rest on the node using the same envelope scheme. For Private/on-prem they never leave your network.
[03:05] Lina (Novus Product): About audit logs — what fields are captured? We need to track user ids, model version, route, request id, timestamp, and optionally redacted prompt hash.
[03:14] Diego: That's our standard schema. We can add a SHA-256 hash of the prompt (salted) for deduplication without storing plaintext. We can also pseudonymize user IDs using your SCIM ids.
[03:24] Samira: Also note we support pushing logs to your SIEM via HTTPS/Syslog. Retention is configurable on your side.
[03:30] Marta: On the \"no training\" side — how do you enforce? Are there internal telemetry pipelines that might leak examples?
[03:36] Ben: We enforce via policy in our data lake — customer data marked as \"no-train\" is excluded from ingestion for any model training. We have attestations, and our engineering change process requires review to enable or change ingestion. We'll give you the list of internal users who have permission for pipeline config.
[03:50] Tom: Can you run a short demo showing a prompt that contains PHI and how it gets pseudonymized in logs?
[03:56] Diego: Yes — we'll demo a sanitized flow after the call with a short video and a sample sanitized audit file. We'll also share a runbook for how to configure the log redaction rules.
[04:06] Rina: If we run a Dedicated pilot, will you keep any copies of the prompt in Redwood-managed storage?
[04:12] Samira: For Dedicated under a reserved capacity contract, default is that logs are retained in Redwood-managed storage for X days for operational health, but we can switch to pushing logs to your storage with 0 retention on our side. For Private, there are no Redwood-managed copies.
[04:25] Jamal: What about function calls / tool calling data — does that get stored differently?
[04:29] Diego: Function call metadata is an independent artifact — we treat it like logs. You can choose to include payloads, or only metadata. We recommend excluding payloads for PHI.
[04:38] Marta: Regarding regulatory controls — if an auditor requests a sample, how do we provide evidence without exposing raw prompts?
[04:44] Ben: We can provide hashed samples, redacted transcripts, and role-scoped audit exports. We also have time-based certificates and logs for retention compliance.
[04:52] Lina: On SSO, do you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[04:55] Samira: Yes, SAML SSO for login, SCIM provisioning for user sync, and fine-grained RBAC roles. We can map your internal teams to Redwood roles and require MFA.
[05:05] Tom: Is there a built-in approval workflow for human-in-the-loop review to prevent accidental access?
[05:09] Priya (CSM): Yes, there's a review workflow and JIT approvals for content access. We can add an additional step for Novus requiring an audit ticket before access is granted.
[05:18] Rina: Let's talk about data residency — can you guarantee that inference happens only in a specific region?
[05:22] Diego: Yes. You can pin model serving to a region/availability zone. For Dedicated we can provision GPU pools in your region; for Hosted API we can route to regional endpoints where available.
[05:31] Jamal: There's a subtlety: logs being pushed to a non-EU bucket could violate residency. We need end-to-end residency — not just inference.
[05:37] Ben: Understood. We'll provide a deployment topology diagram that shows data paths. If you require end-to-end EU residency we can ensure logs, metrics, and backups are all in-region for Dedicated/Private.
[05:48] Marta: On retention policy — typical ask is ephemeral prompt retention of 0-7 days for logs, with an option for 0 days. What are your minimums?
[05:56] Samira: Technically we can do 0 days (no retention) if logs are pushed to your sink and we disable internal retention. For Hosted accounts we generally keep 7 days for debugging, but enterprise contracts can change that.
[06:06] Tom: About the \"no-training\" attestation: do you have audit trails proving pipelines didn't pull data?
[06:11] Ben: Yes. We have change logs, bucket access logs, and data ingestion job logs. We can export a forensic trail demonstrating that a particular dataset was excluded.
[06:20] Rina: If we enable pseudonymization, how reversible is it? We prefer irreversible pseudonymization for PHI.
[06:26] Diego: We support both reversible tokenization (for workflows needing de-id/deanonymize) and irreversible hashing/pseudonymization. You can host the reversible mapping in your KMS-backed vault if you need re-identification.
[06:37] Lina: Will enabling irreversible hashing impact model outputs (e.g., if prompts are hashed, model can't use context)?
[06:42] Diego: Correct. If you hash user-identifying strings in context you'll reduce semantic coherency. For production, we recommend selective pseudonymization — redact PHI, keep structural cues. We'll help design the sanitization rules.
[06:53] Samira: Quick interruption — we heard \"no training\" a few times; that maps to three things: 1) operational logs excluded from training, 2) human review minimization, 3) contractual commitments in DPA. We'll send precise wording.
[07:05] Jamal: Can you show an example event with hashed prompt id vs raw prompt in the audit export?
[07:11] Diego: Yes — we'll attach an example audit JSON and a sample sanitized CSV.
[07:15] Tom: On the legal side, we'll want indemnities tied to data breaches and confirmation of encryption standards (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit).
[07:24] Ben: We use AES-256-GCM for at-rest blobs and TLS1.3 for in-flight. We can confirm versions and cipher suites in the security pack.
[07:30] Rina: One more technical: how do you handle caching between requests for multi-tenant nodes? Could one customer's prefix remain in another customer's node memory?
[07:38] Diego: We enforce tenant isolation at process level. The KV/prefix cache is namespaced by tenant id. For Dedicated pools there's physical isolation on GPU nodes to avoid cross-tenant residue.
[07:49] Marta: For our SOC 2 audit we need to see role lists and last access times for any human reviewer. Can you slice that out?
[07:55] Ben: Yes — we'll provide an access report and proof of JIT approvals.
[07:59] Lina: If we require complete no human review, does that preclude Redwood from debugging incidents?
[08:05] Samira: We can support a mode where Redwood support works with anonymized traces and you run a debug session in a screen share. That avoids sharing raw prompts.
[08:15] Jamal: That's a workable compromise.
[08:18] Tom: About deletion requests — if we ask Redwood to delete retained prompts, what is the SLA and evidence?
[08:23] Samira: Deletion requests have a 72-hour SLA for Hosted; for Dedicated we'll honor immediate deletion in our systems and provide a deletion certificate showing object IDs and timestamps. For Private, you control deletion.
[08:34] Rina: Please clarify what data is considered "customer content" vs "operational metadata" in your contract.
[08:40] Samira: We'll include a mapping in the DPA — generally, prompt/response text is "customer content", token counts and latency are operational metadata. We can mark intermediate embeddings as customer content if you want.
[08:52] Lina: Embeddings are sensitive for us — we treat them like PHI in some flows. Can Redwood avoid storing embeddings or encrypt them with our keys?
[08:59] Diego: Yes — embeddings can be disabled, or stored encrypted with your KMS keys. We can also return embeddings to your sink and not persist them.
[09:07] Marta: One more question about model variants — if a fallback model is used (cheaper model in another region), does data get sent to that model's infrastructure?
[09:15] Ben: Fallback behavior is policy-driven. We can enforce a constraint that no fallback outside a pinned region or variant is allowed for a given tenant.
[09:24] Samira: We're near the end. Quick recap: we'll send SOC2 and security pack, Diego will produce sanitization/config examples and demo video, legal will exchange DPA redlines, and we'll sketch topology for in-region Dedicated. Any other blockers?
[09:37] Marta: Not blocker — just timelines. We need DPA signed before pilot.
[09:41] Samira: Understood. We'll prioritize legal artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[09:46] Tom: Thanks.
[09:47] Diego: We'll follow up with attachments.
[09:50] [call ends at 17:34 PST]
notes: Call included explicit confirmations around no-derivative-training, BYOK KMS support, reversible vs irreversible pseudonymization options, and options to push logs to customer sink for 0-day retention. Customer asked for demo artifacts and DPA redlines prior to pilot.
